caption:
There is a refusal reason that has nothing to do with your money, your job or your itinerary.

Your UAE residence visa expires too soon after your trip.

Consulates want to see that your right to live here extends comfortably past your return date. If it does not, the entire return-to-UAE argument collapses. Renew first, apply second.

slides.headline: CHECK THIS BEFORE YOU CHECK YOUR BANK BALANCE.
slides.sub: It has nothing to do with money.
slides.note: Your UAE residence visa expiring soon after your trip is a refusal reason almost nobody warns you about.

slides.answer: YOUR RETURN CASE RESTS ON IT.
slides.body: The officer is asking whether you will go back to the UAE. If your right to be here is expiring, that answer weakens considerably.
slides.note: They check the expiry date directly. It is not something that gets overlooked.

slides.headline: THE ORDER MATTERS SO MUCH
items: Your entire return argument depends on your residence status
An expiring visa undermines it regardless of everything else
Renewing first costs patience, not money
Applying in the wrong order costs a non-refundable fee

items: Residence visa running well past your return
